newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand needs to tap foreign loans - govt official.
newsitem.headline: Thailand needs to tap foreign loans - govt official.

text.p: A top finance ministry official said on Wednesday the Thai government needs to tap long-term foreign loans to offset recent capital flight and replenish its declining foreign reserves.

Thai finance permanent secretary Chatumongkol Sonukul told reporters Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya instructed him to explore prospects for government offshore borrowing. He did not say how much Thailand would borrow in the near future.
A senior government official said on Tuesday Thailand planned to raise up to $10 billion through loans and government bonds in offshore markets.

"The minister asked us to look into the possibility. The current situation has created a need to borrow after the drain on capital. Long-term loans could offset declined foreign reserves," Chatumongkol said.
Thai foreign reserves fell to a two-year low of $33.3 billion at end-May from $37.4 billion a month earlier after the Bank of Thailand intervened in regional currency markets to defend the baht.
The loss in foreign reserves sharply widened May's balance of payment deficit to 112.3 billion baht ($3.94 billion), a monthly high in several decades and against 15.5 billion baht a month earlier.
Thailand decided to let the baht float on July 2, and since, the currency has dropped more than 15 percent.
The Thai government and state enterprises account for about a quarter of Thailand's $90 billion outstanding foreign debt.
